sorular.soru: Which option correctly states the difference between Continued Pretraining (CPT) and Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT)?
secenekler: CPT learns response tokens from instruction + gold response pairs; SFT predicts the next token on unlabeled raw domain text.
CPT teaches the assistant how it should respond; SFT increases familiarity with the domain's language and terminology.
CPT updates only the embedding layer; SFT updates all Transformer weights and thereby changes response behavior.
CPT predicts the next token on unlabeled domain text; SFT learns response tokens from instruction + gold response pairs.
sorular.aciklama: CPT's data is unlabeled raw domain text with a next-token prediction objective, while SFT's data is instruction + gold response pairs with the objective of predicting the assistant's response tokens. The first option swaps the data and objective of the two methods; CPT increases domain familiarity, whereas SFT teaches response behavior.

sorular.soru: In an SFT example, the model assigns the first response token Positive 30%, Negative 40%, Other 30% probability; the gold target is "Positive". What is the cross-entropy loss at this step?
secenekler: −ln(0.30) ≈ 1.20; the loss is computed only from the gold token's probability
−ln(0.40) ≈ 0.92; the loss is computed from the token with the highest probability
−ln(0.40 − 0.30) ≈ 2.30; the loss measures the difference between prediction and target
−ln(0.30) − ln(0.30) ≈ 2.41; Positive and Other are penalized together
sorular.aciklama: Cross-entropy is the negative logarithm of the probability assigned to the gold token (Positive): −ln(0.30) ≈ 1.20. Negative receiving a higher probability does not enter the formula directly; because the model puts more probability on a wrong token, the gold token's probability stays low and the loss is therefore high.

sorular.konu: Fine-Tuning Data Format and Instruction Tuning
sorular.soru: In a chat-format instruction tuning record (system / user / assistant), which part is the learning target on which the loss is computed?
secenekler: The system message, because it defines the model's behavioral instruction
The user message, because it contains the actual text to be classified
The assistant message, because it is the response expected to be generated
The combination of all three messages, because they are in the same training record
sorular.aciklama: The system message is the behavioral instruction, the user message is the request, and the assistant message is the target response; the assistant response is the learning target. Treating the whole record as the target would turn SFT into next-token prediction on raw text (i.e., CPT), whereas the loss is computed over the tokens of the gold assistant response.

sorular.soru: When an autoregressive LLM and BERT are compared on the same sentiment classification task, which statement is correct?
secenekler: BERT generates the label token by token; the LLM feeds the [CLS] representation to a classification head
The LLM generates the label as text; BERT maps the [CLS] representation to a class via a head
Both use causal attention; the only difference is the [CLS]/[SEP] markers added to the input format
In the LLM the loss is computed over the correct class, in BERT over the generated label tokens only
sorular.aciklama: The LLM, with decoder-only / causal attention, generates the label "Positive" as tokens and the loss is computed on the target response tokens; BERT, with encoder-only / bidirectional attention, predicts the class through [CLS] → classification head and does not generate label text. The third option is wrong because BERT uses bidirectional attention; the last option swaps where the losses are computed.

sorular.soru: An engineer plans to reduce training memory by freezing W₀. Which memory component does freezing NOT eliminate?
secenekler: The Adam momentum and variance states kept for every weight of W₀
The parameter gradients computed for every weight of W₀
The intermediate activation tensors stored for backprop
The need to store a separate full fine-tuned checkpoint per task
sorular.aciklama: Freezing W₀ removes its optimizer states and parameter gradients, but "not all activation memory"; the intermediate activations from the forward pass are still stored for the adapters' gradients. Checkpoint storage (the last option) is a storage cost rather than training memory, and it is already reduced by freezing.

sorular.konu: PEFT and the LoRA Mechanism (W₀, A, B)
sorular.soru: Which statement correctly describes the relationship between SFT and PEFT?
secenekler: SFT fixes the behavior to be learned, PEFT fixes the parameters to be updated; the two can be combined
SFT and PEFT are alternatives to each other; training with PEFT no longer needs instruction + response pairs
PEFT is applied only in the pretraining stage, whereas SFT is applied only in the later adaptation stage
SFT can be done only with full fine-tuning; PEFT methods such as LoRA are suitable only for CPT, not SFT
sorular.aciklama: SFT is defined by the question "what behavior should the model learn?" and PEFT by "which parameters should be updated?": one concerns the data/objective, the other the set of parameters to update, and SFT with LoRA is a combination of the two (only A/B are updated with the SFT loss). Treating PEFT as an alternative to SFT is wrong; even with PEFT, the training data remains instruction + gold response pairs.

sorular.konu: PEFT and the LoRA Mechanism (W₀, A, B)
sorular.soru: Which statement is correct about W₀ in the LoRA formula W′ = W₀ + (α/r)BA?
secenekler: It is a combined weight table representing all 7B+ parameters of the model as a single large matrix
It is a single projection matrix in one layer; each target projection has its own W₀ and A/B pair
It is a matrix randomly initialized in pretraining and updated together with A/B during SFT
It is a low-rank update obtained from the product of A and B and coming from the pretraining checkpoint
sorular.aciklama: W₀ is a single pretrained projection matrix (e.g., a 3584×3584 q_proj in Qwen2.5-7B) and "does not represent all 7B+ parameters"; each selected projection has its own frozen W₀ and its own A/B pair. Mistaking W₀ for the whole model is a common error; the low-rank update is BA, not W₀.

sorular.konu: PEFT and the LoRA Mechanism (W₀, A, B)
sorular.soru: In LoRA, A is initialized randomly and B to zero. Which statement is correct about the gradient flow in the first training step?
secenekler: Both matrices receive zero gradient; learning begins only after a few steps through random noise
A receives a gradient and B's gradient is zero; because A is applied to the input x first
Since BA = 0, a copy of W₀ is written into B and A is reinitialized
B receives a gradient and A's gradient is zero; once B moves away from zero, A also starts learning
sorular.aciklama: Initially BA = 0, so W′ = W₀; in the first update B receives a gradient, while A's gradient is zero because B = 0; once B moves away from zero, both matrices learn. The second option is intuitive but reversed: A's gradient flows through B, so it is zero while B is zero; applying A to x first does not determine the order of the gradient.

sorular.konu: LoRA Hyperparameters: r, α, Dropout, Target Modules
sorular.soru: LoRA with r = 2 is used on a 4×4 layer. If α is raised from 2 to 4, how do the number of trainable parameters and the update change?
secenekler: The parameter count rises from 16 to 32; the update's scale (α/r) stays unchanged
The parameter count rises from 8 to 16; the update is scaled from ×1 to ×2
The parameter count stays at 16; the update (α/r)BA is scaled from ×1 to ×2
The parameter count stays at 16; the update (α/r)BA is scaled from ×1 to ×4
sorular.aciklama: For r = 2, A (2×4) and B (4×2) give 16 trainable values in total; α only changes the factor (α/r): α = 2 → ×1, α = 4 → ×2. The last option forgets to divide α by r; the first option assumes α adds parameters, whereas "changing α alone does not add trainable parameters".

sorular.konu: LoRA Hyperparameters: r, α, Dropout, Target Modules
sorular.soru: For a 3584×3584 q_proj in Qwen2.5-7B, LoRA with r = 8 gives 57,344 trainable parameters (≈224× reduction). What happens if r = 16 is chosen for the same projection?
secenekler: ≈114,688 parameters; the reduction ratio drops to ≈112×
≈57,344 parameters remain; r only changes the scale of the update
≈229,376 parameters; both dimensions of A and B double
≈28,672 parameters; a single matrix suffices for a higher r
sorular.aciklama: A: r×din = 16×3584 = 57,344 and B: dout×r = 3584×16 = 57,344, for a total of 114,688; 12,845,056 / 114,688 ≈ 112. The parameter count grows linearly with r (only one dimension of each matrix is r), so it doubles rather than quadrupling (229,376); the idea that r is only a scale factor confuses it with α.

sorular.konu: LoRA Hyperparameters: r, α, Dropout, Target Modules
sorular.soru: Which statement about LoRA hyperparameters is correct?
secenekler: LoRA dropout is applied during training to the output of the frozen W₀ branch
Target modules can be only attention projections; FFN projections cannot be selected
Increasing α, like increasing r, increases the number of parameters in the A/B matrices
LoRA dropout is applied during training only to the adapter (A/B) branch
sorular.aciklama: LoRA dropout "applies to the adapter branch during training", i.e., to the A/B branch and not to the frozen W₀ path. Target modules can include k_proj, o_proj, and the FFN projections in addition to q_proj and v_proj; α only changes the (α/r) scale and adds no parameters.

sorular.soru: A company wants legal, medical, and finance assistants built from the same base model. With LoRA, which is the most efficient storage and loading strategy?
secenekler: Store a separate full fine-tuned checkpoint for each domain; load the relevant full model at use time
Store W₀ once and save an A/B pair per domain; at use time load the desired adapter via W₀ + (α/r)BA
Combine the data of all three domains and train a single A/B; still store W₀ separately for each domain
Re-pretrain W₀ from scratch for each domain; share the A/B pairs in common across the three domains
sorular.aciklama: The base checkpoint W₀ is stored once, a small A/B pair is kept separately for each domain, and the desired adapter is loaded via W₀ + (α/r)BA. Storing a full checkpoint per domain is expensive in storage; LoRA's advantage is precisely that it avoids this.

sorular.soru: Which memory problem does LoRA not solve, but QLoRA directly targets?
secenekler: The optimizer states of the A/B adapters taking up a lot of GPU memory
The gradients of the trainable parameters being recomputed at every step
The frozen W₀ still occupying a lot of memory in FP16/BF16
The adapter checkpoints saved per domain growing larger and larger
sorular.aciklama: "LoRA saves optimizer/gradient memory, but the frozen model is still large"; QLoRA targets this problem by storing the frozen base in 4-bit NF4 (≈15.2 GB → ≈3.8 GB for 7.6B parameters). The optimizer states of A/B are already small; that is a cost LoRA has already solved.

sorular.soru: If a weight of 0.46 is encoded and decoded with a symmetric uniform quantizer (s = 0.1; z = 0), what are the stored code and the dequantized value?
secenekler: Code 5, value 0.50; approximation error 0.04
Code 4, value 0.40; approximation error 0.06
Code 5, value 0.46; approximation error zero
Code 46, value 0.46; approximation error zero
sorular.aciklama: Encode: q = round(0.46 / 0.1) = round(4.6) = 5; decode: ŵ = 5 × 0.1 = 0.50; error |0.46 − 0.50| = 0.04 (the same steps as in the 0.73 → 7 → 0.70 example). The code 4 option truncates downward instead of rounding; lossless recovery of the original value is not possible in quantization.

sorular.soru: Which statement is correct about the difference between NF4 (NormalFloat 4-bit) and uniform 4-bit quantization?
secenekler: NF4 uses more code values (32); so it is much more precise at the same bit count
Both use 16 codes; NF4 places its levels more densely where the weights concentrate
NF4 encodes every weight with a fixed scale in steps of 0.1; uniform uses a block scale
In NF4 too, 0.73 → code 7 → 0.70 is decoded; only the way the codes are stored differs
sorular.aciklama: Both methods have 16 code values, but while uniform levels are equally spaced, NF4 uses a nonuniform codebook with "unequal spacing; more levels where weights are concentrated" and normalizes values with a block scale. Note that the code 7 / 0.70 mapping from the uniform example does not carry over to NF4.

sorular.soru: Which statement is correct about the computation performed with the frozen NF4 weights during the forward pass in QLoRA?
secenekler: Matrix multiplication is performed directly in 4-bit integer arithmetic; the memory savings come from this
A full 16-bit copy of W₀ is kept in memory; NF4 is only for disk storage
A and B are also quantized to NF4; so gradients are stored in 4-bit
Weights are dequantized to BF16/FP16 and then multiplied; the savings come from 4-bit storage
sorular.aciklama: 4-bit storage is not 4-bit computation: the NF4 weights are dequantized for computation and the multiplication is done in BF16/FP16; the memory savings come from 4-bit storage because no full 16-bit copy is kept. A/B remain trainable in BF16/FP16, and backprop updates only them.

sorular.soru: A researcher believes some layers need more adaptation capacity than others and wants how much rank each layer gets to be determined automatically during training. Which variant targets this?
secenekler: QLoRA — stores the frozen base in NF4 and devotes the freed memory to the adapters
DoRA — decomposes the weight into magnitude and direction components and adapts the direction with LoRA
AdaLoRA — adaptively distributes a limited total rank budget across layers
LoRA — adds a low-rank correction with the same r value in all target projections
sorular.aciklama: AdaLoRA (Zhang et al., 2023) "adaptively distribute a limited rank budget across layers" — for example, different ranks such as r = 1/4/2 are assigned to layers 1/2/3. DoRA separates magnitude and direction (direction via LoRA), and QLoRA only changes how the base is stored; neither touches rank allocation.

sorular.soru: After fine-tuning, training accuracy is measured at 99% and test accuracy at 65%. What is the appropriate first interpretation of this picture?
secenekler: The model has generalized successfully; one should now move on to tuning hyperparameters on the test set
Overfitting, data leakage, or data shift should be investigated
r should be lowered; high training accuracy is always caused by too many adapter parameters
The test set should be added to training and the model retrained, then measured again on the same test set
sorular.aciklama: The 99% train / 65% test gap points to a generalization problem; overfitting, leakage, or data shift should be investigated. Hyperparameters are chosen on the validation set and the test set is used only once, for the final evaluation; therefore tuning on the test set or adding it to training breaks the process.
